page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ds_v5 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It utilizes an x86_64 architecture with 48 MB of L3 cache, supporting AVX-512 vector extensions and VAES cryptographic acceleration. The instance is paired with 672 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory allocation of 28 GB per vCPU, and includes 3,865 GB of local NVMe SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark results reflect the memory-focused hardware architecture. The instance shows strong memory throughput, scoring in the top 25% for PassMark memory (2,879.74) and achieving 108.01 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory writes. General computing and integer throughput tests, such as Geekbench multi-core (12,266.0) and stress-ng multi-core (23,302.71), place within the middle 50% across measured cloud instances. Because CPU core count is constrained relative to the full 96-vCPU chassis, highly parallel CPU-bound tasks like 70B parameter LLM inference exhibit poor performance (4.85 tokens/sec).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained vCPU ratio provides distinct economic advantages for software licensed per core, such as relational database engines. Workloads that require massive working memory and fast local scratch space can operate without incurring software licensing fees for unneeded cores. Tradeoffs include reduced compute parallelism compared to standard instances with equivalent total memory footprints.

The E96-24ds_v5 is suitable for memory-intensive relational database management systems like Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle Database, large in-memory caching solutions like Redis, intermediate data engineering pipelines, and memory-bound analytics tasks that benefit from the 3,865 GB local SSD.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-dense enterprise workloads requiring restricted CPU core counts. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor, the instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 672 GB of memory (28 GB per vCPU), and 3,865 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. In benchmark testing, the instance registers strong memory throughput, scoring in the top quartile for PassMark memory and large-block write bandwidth, while general compute and compression metrics remain average. The constrained vCPU topology optimizes software licensing costs for applications billed on a per-core basis without sacrificing memory capacity. With no integrated GPUs and average parallel compute throughput, this instance is suited for relational database engines, large Redis caches, memory-bound analytics, and data pipeline intermediate storage.
